candidates.hypothesis: Long long-dated Treasury futures during the New York session of the trading day before the Treasury's quarterly refunding Primary Release (pre-TRA day, usually a Friday); flat by 15:05 CT
candidates.mechanism: resolution of fiscal/Treasury-market uncertainty before the quarterly refunding announcement (term-premium compression; authors' uncertainty-reduction channel)
candidates.entry_window_ct: 06:30 CT (07:30 ET, NY open) or 17:00 CT session open of the pre-TRA trading day; exit <= 15:05 CT
candidates.best_source: Wang, Zhao, Pre-Refunding Announcement Gains in U.S. Treasurys, draft July 16 2025 (first version March 18 2024), OSF preprint xucf8
candidates.sample: CRSP daily Treasury returns 1991Q4-2023 (129 pre-TRA days); Tradeweb minute quotes 2006-2023 for intraday
candidates.post_2015_or_oos: post-2002 subsample 10-year 15.48 bp (t 3.27, N 88) includes 2015-2023; no out-of-sample or post-2023 replication found; research window 2025-04..2026-06 (about 5 events) is post-publication
candidates.published_effect: 10-year cash Treasury +12.62 bp on pre-TRA days (daily close-to-close, sd 43.15, N 129, t 3.32); intraday: '10-year Treasury rising by over 10 bps' in the NY morning; 30-year +24.33 bp; 5-year +8.25 bp
candidates.price_level_used: ZN 110 (1 tick = 1.42 bp); ZN price change = 0.69 x 10-year cash (E.20 assumption)
candidates.micro: none (no micro 10-year note; 1 ZN = $15.625/tick). ZN ticks: 6.13 (daily mean), 4.86 (intraday >10 bp lower bound), 4.19 (non-ZLB 8.62 bp)
candidates.dispersion: per-event sd 43.15 bp (cash 10-year), about 21 ZN ticks; t 3.32; N 129; strategy Sharpe 4.50 (10-year, annualized, 4 trades/yr, gross)
candidates.quote: A significant upward price movement in Treasurys begins early in the New York trading session on the day preceding the TRA (Day −1). Prices increase notably in the morning, with the 10-year Treasury rising by over 10 bps, and then continue to increase marginally for the remainder of New York trading hours.
candidates.quote_location: Section 4.3, p. 19; Table 2 Panel A; Table 6
candidates.decay_evidence: none reported; effect larger after 2002 (10-year 6.48 bp pre-2002 vs 15.48 post-2002); weak in downward-sloping curve (4.71, t 0.36, N 10), Q2 (-2.81), recessions (-2.18)
candidates.data_needed: ZN/ZB/UB/ZF 1-minute bars (owned); TRA (Primary Release) dates from Treasury quarterly refunding press releases (public, free; not in owned calendars; paper's Table 1 lists 1991-2023)
candidates.data_cost: TRA dates free (home.treasury.gov press releases; terms not checked by RD2); bars owned
candidates.why: ZN is in the research window, but only about 5 pre-TRA days fall in 2025-04..2026-06; 2010-2024 owned bars give about 55 events
candidates.prop_notes: flat by 15:05 CT; pre-TRA Fridays can be NFP Fridays or month-end days: P06 caps size into scheduled major releases; no micro, 1 ZN minimum; 4 trades a year cannot carry Topstep consistency rules alone
candidates.overlap_note: no member uses TRA dates; partial date overlap with month-end members (paper controls EOM and effect survives); auction-cycle members trade the following week's auctions

candidates.hypothesis: Long ZN from 19:00 ET on day -2 (Tokyo open, the evening before a scheduled FOMC meeting's first day) to 12:00 ET on day -1 (London close)
candidates.mechanism: pre-FOMC risk-premium (term-premium) drift in long-term Treasuries realized during Asian and London hours, earlier than the equity pre-FOMC drift
candidates.entry_window_ct: 18:00 CT on day -2 (start of Topstep trading day for day -1); exit 11:00 CT day -1
candidates.hold: 17 h inside one Topstep trading day
candidates.best_source: Pan, Peng, The Pre-FOMC Drift in Long-Term Treasury Bonds, SAIF draft June 2 2026 (first draft May 31 2023)
candidates.sample: 10-year Treasury note futures intraday 2004-01..2025-06; daily zero-coupon yields 1994-09..2025-12, 250 scheduled FOMC announcements
candidates.post_2015_or_oos: sample runs to 2025-06; no separate post-2015 intraday figure; excluding 2008-2009 daily 10-year yield -0.70 (t -2.29); no independent replication found
candidates.published_effect: 'The average 10-year Treasury return over this non-U.S. trading window is approximately 7.26 basis points, with a statistically significant t-statistic of 2.82'; rest of day -1 (12:00-17:00 ET) -2.05 bp (t -1.76); daily 10-year zero yield -0.79 bp (t -2.39)
candidates.micro: none (1 ZN). ZN ticks: 5.11 if 7.26 bp is a ZN futures return (Figure 2 plots 10-year note futures); 3.53 if a cash 10-year return (x 0.69)
candidates.dispersion: t 2.82 over about 170 meetings (2004-2025, count not stated for the intraday sample); per-event sd not published
candidates.quote: The average cumulative return on U.S. Treasury futures begins to rise at 19:00 ET on day -2, coinciding with the start of the Tokyo market, and peaks at 12:00 ET on day -1, aligning with the closing of the London market. The average 10-year Treasury return over this non-U.S. trading window is approximately 7.26 basis points, with a statistically significant t-statistic of 2.82.
candidates.decay_evidence: regime-dependent: authors link it to 'the post-2008 QE environment'; QE3 dummy positive (yield up) 0.84/1.92**; Lucca-Moench's 2pm-to-2pm window shows nothing; window chosen ex post from the figure
candidates.data_needed: ZN 1-minute bars including the overnight session (owned, Globex ohlcv-1m); FOMC statement dates (owned)
candidates.why: ZN and FOMC dates in the research window (about 10 meetings 2025-04..2026-06; partly inside the paper's sample to 2025-06)
candidates.prop_notes: entry 18:00 CT is in the overnight session; exit 11:00 CT; flat well before 15:10 CT; day -1 can coincide with 07:30 CT releases (CPI etc.): P06; overnight liquidity and cost outside D8's day-session bucket [unverified]
candidates.overlap_note: tested FOMC members trade day 0 (statement day) on rates, MES or MGC; none holds rates on day -1
